Ridiculously priced
Oct 2025 • Family
I dined at Masala Art on a Wednesday evening, drawn by its reputed authenticity and central location. While I must acknowledge that the service was courteous and the food itself competently prepared, the establishment’s pricing structure left me thoroughly disillusioned.
To illustrate: a single piece of masala papadam is priced at an astonishing VND 70,000/- (approximately USD 2.66) a figure that borders on the absurd for what is essentially a humble appetizer. I ordered it nonetheless, more out of curiosity than indulgence, but the sense of being blatantly overcharged overshadowed any appreciation of its taste.
Similarly, the paneer tikka—though flavorful—was served in a disappointingly modest portion that hardly justified its premium cost. In a city like Hanoi, where one can find numerous Indian restaurants offering authentic, high-quality fare at far more reasonable prices, Masala Art’s pricing feels not just ambitious but exploitative.
To be clear, my critique lies solely with the value for money—the cuisine and service were respectable, but the exorbitant prices render the overall experience unsatisfactory. Unless one has a particular inclination toward paying luxury prices for standard Indian dishes, I would strongly advise seeking out other establishments in Hanoi that offer both quality and fairness.
In conclusion, Masala Art may satisfy the palate, but it grievously offends the sense of proportion. A restaurant that aspires to fine dining must understand that refinement lies not in overpricing, but in offering a balance between quality, quantity, and value. Two stars are taken away only for their pricing.

Manchester, United Kingdom589 contributions

Good Food Bad Experience
Jun 2024 • Couples
Arrived soaking wet after running through a major thunderstorm. The manager on the desk just looked up and said sit as if we were a couple of dogs. Didn't even ask us if we had a reservation which we had. Not a good start. The restraunt is nicely decorated. The food is excellent and the two young waiters who served us were great. Halfway through our meal a tour of over 20 Indian men arrived and started to queue for the toilets all around our table. They even started to take paper napkins off our table interrupting our meal. The manager said nothing. In the end one of the younger waiters told them off and told them to move. They then stood around staring at us because they wanted to sit at our table. This turned our meal into a bad experience so we left. Tour groups should be kept to a reserved part of the restraunt and not left to upset other diners. Wouldn't recommend this restraunt for a relaxing experience. We will go elsewhere on our next visit to Hanoi.
